fields.features_heading: What the Booth Records Before Visitors Leave
fields.features_subheading: Paper lead sheets sit in a box until someone types them up. Describe your booth, and Emergent builds the form and its database.
fields.feature_1:
A rating set before the visitor walks away

Booth staff pick hot, warm, or cold and add when the visitor plans to buy. The rating and the buying timeline stay on the lead, and the rep reads both before making the first call.
fields.feature_2:
Business cards read into the right fields

Photograph a card on the tablet and the app reads the name, title, company, and email into the form. Any field it cannot read clearly goes back to the staffer to type in by hand.
fields.feature_3:
Hot leads sent to the rep for the territory

Match the visitor's state to a sales territory and send each hot lead to that rep in Slack or by email. Warm and cold leads wait in the database for follow-up after the show.
fields.feature_4:
One form for every show on the calendar

Each lead carries the show name and the staffer who took it. A live dashboard counts leads and hot leads for each show, and marketing compares a whole season of events side by side.
fields.feature_5:
Leads that reach your CRM tagged by show

Connect HubSpot or any CRM with an API, and each saved lead syncs over with its rating and show tag. Reps work the list where they already work, with no spreadsheet import.
fields.feature_6:
Code export for a lead system you keep

On paid plans, export the full codebase to your GitHub repository and host the lead form wherever you want. Keep building on it between shows, or hand it to your own developers.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Exhibitors Work Their Leads
fields.tab_content_1:
For an Ohio buyer 90 days out, Leopoldo gets a message

Kestrelford Pumps staffs a water treatment expo with tablets, and each visitor gets a rating and buying timeline. A hot lead buying within 90 days goes to the rep for that state. Brinmoor Water District in Ohio plans to buy in 60 days, and Midwest rep Leopoldo Vorstman gets a Slack direct message before the buyer leaves.
fields.tab_content_2:
One blurred number on the card goes back to Zephyrine

Lindqvane Software's booth staff photograph business cards instead of typing. At a developer conference, Zephyrine Elsbury scans the card of Lisandro Quintavalle from Tarnhollow Freight. The app fills in his name, title, company, and email, but the phone number is blurred. Zephyrine confirms it before the lead saves.
fields.tab_content_3:
Of 148 leads from Gulf Coast, 9 were hot

Stoneleigh Packaging works three shows in the fall, and every lead carries its show. Ambrosine Corbishley in marketing reads the dashboard. Lakeshore Pack Show brought 212 leads with 41 hot, and Northeast Retail Fair 96 with 22 hot. Gulf Coast Food Expo brought 148 with only 9 hot, and goes on her review list.
fields.tab_content_4:
Each hot lead with no call after 2 days reaches Isidore

Every lead from Abernant Office Furniture's booth syncs to HubSpot tagged with its show, and reps log calls there. Two days after the show closes, any hot lead with no logged call goes on the follow-up list. This week Isidore Pennefather in sales operations gets an email naming 3 leads and each one's rep.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Trade Show Lead Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a trade show lead form template that rates each visitor and alerts the rep who owns the territory.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Ask reps what they need for a first call
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Map each state to a rep
fields.howto_step_1_des: Ask your reps what they need before calling a lead back: the visitor's role, the product they stopped for, and when they plan to buy. Those become the questions on the form. Anything a rep never reads after a show comes off it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Limit the questions staff ask face to face to what fits a short conversation in a busy aisle. Contact details come from the business card, and the staffer adds the rating and a line of notes while the visitor is still standing there.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write down what each rating means, such as hot for a buyer with a budget and a date inside 90 days. Staff on different shifts then rate visitors the same way, and reps trust the label they see on each lead when they open it.
fields.howto_step_4_des: List which rep owns each state or region and how they want to hear about hot leads: a Slack direct message, an email, or both. Warm and cold leads skip the alert and wait in the database for the campaign after the show.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Tag every lead with the show
fields.howto_step_5_des: Set the show name as a hidden field before the doors open, along with the name of the staffer on shift. When the season ends, those tags let marketing compare shows by total leads and hot leads instead of by memory.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Connect the CRM your reps use
fields.howto_step_6_des: Name the CRM and the fields it expects, and Emergent connects the form to it through the CRM's API. Then decide how many days reps get before an uncalled hot lead goes on a follow-up list, and who receives that list.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Run the form on the booth tablets the day before the show opens. Scan 5 real business cards, rate a few test visitors, and confirm each alert reaches the right rep. Clear the test leads from the database before the first real visitor.

faq_plan.q: What is a trade show lead form template?
faq_plan.a: A trade show lead form template is a reusable form booth staff fill in for each visitor they talk to at an exhibit. It records who the visitor is, what they asked about, how close they are to buying, and which show they came from. Sales then works the follow-up from those records.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a trade show lead form template?
faq_plan.a: Describe your booth and your follow-up in a prompt, and Emergent's AI form builder builds the form with its lead rating and the database behind it. Ask for the rep alerts and the CRM connection in the same prompt, then change any question later by asking for the change.

faq_plan.q: What questions should a trade show lead form template ask?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the visitor's name, company, role, and email. Then ask which product they came to see and their buying timeline. Add a rating and a notes line for the staffer. Save deeper questions, such as budget detail or contract dates, for the first sales call.

faq_plan.q: Should booth staff or visitors fill in a trade show lead form template?
faq_plan.a: Booth staff should fill in the qualifying part. A website lead capture form is filled in by the visitor alone. At a booth, the staffer adds fields a visitor never sees, such as the rating and notes on what was discussed. Visitors can still type their own email on the tablet.

faq_plan.q: How should booth staff rate leads on a trade show lead form template?
faq_plan.a: Give staff three ratings with written rules, and tie each one to something the visitor said, such as a purchase date or a budget. Put the rule next to the rating on the form. Two staffers who meet the same visitor should then pick the same rating.

faq_plan.q: Can a trade show lead form template read business cards?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The app Emergent builds can read a photographed business card into structured contact fields with AI. Any field it reads with low confidence is sent to the staffer to check, and the staffer can type a field by hand when a card has no email.

faq_plan.q: How do I get leads from a trade show lead form template into my CRM?
faq_plan.a: Connect the form to your CRM through its API, and each lead arrives there with the booth rating and the staffer's notes attached. With Emergent, every lead also lives in a database you own. Match the field names to the CRM before the show, not after.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a trade show lead form template have?
faq_plan.a: Keep it to five or six questions beyond the contact details. Visitors stop at a booth for a short conversation, and staff fill the form while they talk. Rehearse it on the booth tablet and cut any question staff skip twice.

faq_plan.q: Can I use one trade show lead form template for every show?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Keep one form and set the show name before each event, and every lead carries the show it came from. Change a question for one show by prompting for it. The form Emergent builds has no response cap, however many shows the season holds.

faq_plan.q: What happens to leads from a trade show lead form template after the show?
faq_plan.a: They go where your rules send them. Send each hot lead to its rep the same day, with the notes from the booth. Move warm leads into an email sequence and cold leads onto the newsletter list. Set a deadline for the first call on every hot lead, and report on the ones that miss it.

faq_heading: Trade Show Lead Form Template FAQ

plan.angle: The results for this query are printable lead sheets (Word, PDF, a stapler for business cards) and form-tool template pages that stop at the fields. None shows what happens after the badge conversation: a rating the booth staff set, a business card read into fields, the hot lead reaching the rep for that territory before the visitor leaves the hall, leads compared across a season of shows, and the handoff into the CRM. This page shows a working trade show lead form at four booths, every lead saved to a database the exhibitor owns. No claims about any show, badge scanner or CRM beyond the approved API connection.
